title: Feedback Is Everything
equation: Improvement = Feedback Speed × Willingness to Adjust
hook: Tracking everything and changing nothing is just a really organized way of staying stuck.
statement: Systems that don't measure can't improve.
explainer: Without a number you check, you're guessing. And even with the number, it only helps if you actually change something when it tells you to.
sop: Pick the one number that shows whether this system works.
Track it weekly. A basic spreadsheet is fine.
Score your Feedback Speed and Willingness to Adjust 1 to 10.
Block 15 minutes a week to actually look at it.
Change one thing based on the number, even if your gut disagrees.
equation_example: Feedback Speed 7, Willingness to Adjust 4. 7 × 4 = 28 out of 100. Higher means you're getting signal and acting on it. Fast signal with low willingness means you're measuring everything and changing nothing.
question: Name one thing you're trying to improve that you aren't actually measuring yet.
closing_statement: What you don't measure stays the same.
caption:
Principle Nº 104: Feedback Is Everything

Tracking everything and changing nothing is just a really organized way of staying stuck.

Systems that don't measure can't improve.

Your turn: Name one thing you're trying to improve that you aren't actually measuring yet.
